questions.question_text: Explain the Data-Information-Knowledge pyramid and the differences between data, information, and knowledge.
questions.model_answer: The Data-Information-Knowledge pyramid shows a hierarchy from raw data at the bottom to knowledge at the top. Data is the representation of facts or ideas in a suitable format for storage, processing, or transmission (e.g., numbers, figures, statistics). It is unstructured, has no dependencies, and is derived from user or system inputs. Information is processed, organized, and structured data that provides context and enables decision making. It has a logical structure, is presented through reports and graphs, depends on data, and is derived from data processing. Knowledge is our understanding of the world—an appropriate collection of information that makes it useful. It answers how and why questions, provides the ability to predict and make decisions, and requires learning of the subject. Information becomes knowledge when critical thinking, evaluation, structure, or organization is applied.

questions.question_text: Compare Data Science and Business Intelligence in terms of scope, tools, data types, complexity, and flexibility.
questions.model_answer: Data Science uses data to make future forecasts for business development, while Business Intelligence analyzes past data to understand current business trends. Data Science includes complex algorithmic models, data processing, and big data tools, whereas BI tools are limited to analyzing management information and overseeing business strategies. Data Science works with structured data but mainly deals with unstructured and semi-structured data, while BI works with structured data typically stored in data warehouses. Data Science has more complexity compared to BI, which is much simpler. Data Science is much more flexible as data sources can be added as required, while BI is less flexible as data sources must be pre-designed.

questions.question_text: Describe the five stages of the Data Science Life Cycle and the purpose of each stage.
questions.model_answer: The five stages are: 1) Problem Definition and Formulation: Understanding the objectives and requirements of a business or scientific problem and converting this knowledge into a data analysis problem. 2) Data Collection: The process of gathering and measuring data, including data acquisition, data labeling, and data improvement. 3) Data Preparation and Cleaning: The multistage process of reviewing and correcting data to ensure it is in a standardized format, including handling missing values, smoothing noisy data, and resolving inconsistencies and duplicates. 4) Exploratory Data Analysis: The approach to analyzing datasets to summarize their main characteristics, often using visual methods. 5) Data Visualization: A graphical representation of information that highlights patterns and trends in data and aids the reader in gaining quick insights.

questions.question_text: Explain the five characteristics of Big Data: Volume, Variety, Velocity, Veracity, and Value.
questions.model_answer: Volume: Because large volumes of low-density, unstructured data must be handled, the amount of data is a critical aspect. This can be tens of terabytes or hundreds of petabytes. Variety: Refers to the many different types of data available, including structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data types (such as text, audio, and video) that require additional preprocessing to derive meaning. Velocity: The rate at which data is captured and stored. Most internet-connected smart devices and mobile devices work in real-time or near real-time, requiring instant data collection, transmission, and storage. Veracity: Has to do with how accurate or truthful a dataset may be—not just the quality of the data itself but how trustworthy the data source, type, and processing is. Value: Just because we collected lots of data does not mean it is of any value; value refers to how useful the data is in decision making. We need to extract the value of the big data using proper analytics.

questions.question_text: Explain the steps of Knowledge Discovery in data mining, as presented in the lecture.
questions.model_answer: The steps of Knowledge Discovery are: 1) Data cleaning: Clean corrupt data, irregularities, false data types, etc. 2) Data integration: Merge data from multiple sources into a single dataset. 3) Data selection: Select the part of the dataset most representative of your goals, since data mining is time-consuming. 4) Data transformation: Prepare and format raw datasets so that data mining processes have inputs in the required format. 5) Data mining: The actual process of analyzing the data and extracting desired results through patterns. 6) Pattern evaluation: Decode the patterns generated by data mining and decide which are beneficial for each specific goal. 7) Knowledge representation: Visualize the generated results with clear and concise reports, graphs, and plots.
